subject: Sprint velocity constraints, dependent services tradeoffs, and escalation plan
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-prod@acme.com, procurement@acme.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sprint velocity constraints, dependent services tradeoffs, and escalation plan

Team —

As we prep the QBR pack this week I want a short, actionable snapshot of where product & eng stand against the June->July launch commitments. TL;DR: velocity is below plan by ~18% on core shipping stories, and two external dependencies are likely to push the critical path beyond our soft launch window unless we take mitigations.

Key asks (please respond by EOD):
- Karthik: brief note on the infra backlog items blocking autoscaling tests (specifically: job #4123 and #4130). Can we get a firm ETA or do we need a carve-out?
- Laura: update the risk register with current exposure (impact x probability) and call out any new cross-team blockers from PM/UX.
- Tessa: outline 2 contingency trajectories (A: reduce scope, B: delayed non-essential features + extended hardening) with estimated impact on ARR and customer experience.

Attachments: QBR_Risk_Register_v3.xlsx (current scoring), Launch_Timeline_V2.pdf (proposed dates + milestones). I27ve included Acme procurement & platform leads FYI — they asked for a heads up on any timeline shifts that would affect the beta contract.

Notes from my read:
- Perf regression on the streaming path adds ~30ms tail latency under 95th percentile when sequence length >1024; we27re seeing a ~12% throughput drop when batching more aggressively to save cost.
- Third-party partner (real-time metrics pipeline) still unresolved on certs; their SLA gating is the larger risk.

I27ll consolidate replies and put a single-slide summary in the QBR deck.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

--

Attachment: Launch_Timeline_V2.pdf (pdf, 210KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprint velocity constraints, dependent services tradeoffs, and escalation plan

Vanessa —

Short update from infra/runtime: job #4123 (kv cache invalidation race) is currently triaged; root cause is a regression introduced in the 2027-06-10 kernel shuffle that only reproduces at scale. We have a small team (2 ICs + 1 SRE) working on a fix; estimated patch ETA is 2027-07-05, testing complete by 2027-07-07 if nothing unexpected pops up.

Job #4130 (autoscale stress harness) requires partner cert access to run full throughput sweeps — that27s the gating item. If we can get a temporary allowlist from the partner for our test CIDRs we can run limited sweeps earlier (target 2027-07-01).

Options:
A) Carve out a hotspot fix (1wk) and fall back to single-node mode for a controlled ramp — lower performance, but keeps launch date.
B) Wait for full fix + partner certs and shift launch by 2 weeks.

My recommendation: pursue the allowlist for immediate testing (option A + parallel full fix); if partner cannot allowlist, we should trigger the two-week shift.

Karthik
Director, Infrastructure & Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Vanessa / Karthik —

Updated the attached risk register with current exposure + mitigation owners (see row highlights):
- "Partner pipeline certs" moved to HIGH probability / CRITICAL impact (owner: Platform Partnerships).
- "Streaming tail latency" re-scored to MEDIUM probability / HIGH impact based on recent perf runs.
- "Engineering hiring gap" added as a medium likelihood item tied to two mid-July leaves.

Two asks for leadership:
1) Approve a soft contingency budget of $40k to run an accelerated test window with the partner (this covers temporary infra burst and no-ops traffic to validate autoscale).
2) Confirm whether we move forward with the minimal-scope launch (feature-cut) cadence or preserve scope and accept a two-week shift. I can add impact rows for both in the QBR slide if you pick one.

I27m tagging procurement & Acme for visibility on contractual slack — procurement asked for one consolidated date option to assess invoicing and support ramp.

Laura Bennett

Folks —

I ran two concise contingency trajectories as requested (high-level):

Trajectory A (minimal scope / keep launch date):
- Cut: non-critical personalization flags, extended analytics dashboard, and one optional reranker.
- Impact: preserves 95% of core UX; estimated ARR impact: -0.6% in Q3.
- Ops: require temporary single-node fallback during day-1 high load windows; documented runbook ready.

Trajectory B (preserve scope / shift by 2 weeks):
- Preservation of full feature set; complete infra patch + partner cert testing window.
- Impact: ARR neutral but delays ramp; additional cost: ~$18k for extended test windows + $10k incident reserves.

Recommended path: Begin with Trajectory A as a canary (announce reduced scope to selected beta customers only) while Karthik tries to secure the allowlist for earlier testing. If partner agree, we restore features for GA.

I27ll draft a one-slide decision matrix for the QBR and send it by EOD Tue.

Tessa Morgan
Senior Program Manager, Product
tessa_morgan@redwood.com

Thanks all — consolidated decision for the QBR pack:

Decision (for leadership review at tomorrow27s QBR):
- Adopt Trajectory A (minimal scope canary) for GA to preserve the launch date but limit exposure.
- Approve the contingency budget request ($40k) to run accelerated partner validation and temporary infra bursts.
- Karthik to continue parallel work on the root-cause patch; if partner allowlist is confirmed by 2027-07-01 we27ll attempt a scope restore before GA.

Irene: please include the contingency budget ask in the executive deck and flag for approval in the finance block. Acme / procurement — thanks for being on standby; procurement, can you confirm whether the one-week shift window would materially change invoicing terms?

I27ll add the single-slide decision matrix and the updated risk register to the QBR folder and share the link.
